passes.notes: Style/retention pass begins: captions are short and object-led, usually name a visible feature then immediately define evidentiary boundary. Preserve model/date negatives (not later device/reissue, no inferred region/spec/performance/function, current condition unknown); these are useful precision, not boilerplate to trim. The M5 photo’s chip/performance caveat and Kindle/iPad version distinctions are especially important because visual resemblance could otherwise overstate what the frame proves. Ericofon date/model wording distinguishes era body from DBJ700; Switch2 performance and battery restraint; HP-65 current function unknown; XEL-1 region power label absent; Kenwood wear is not original finish. Preserve these concise negatives as essential visual-evidence boundaries. Switch Lite/Wii U captions use body/control comparison, with Wii U author edits disclosed; no claim that the full image was untouched. Framework date caveat is a clear example of chronology discipline: Jan 2022 display precedes May Intel 12th-gen announcement, and no CPU claim. Nokia visual is not the referenced O2 handset/reissue; Osborne shows task layout; PSVR is pre-ZVR2 but not retail kit/firmware. Music-machine descriptions are restrained to panels/controls; repeated generic “contact sheet” notes are workflow metadata rather than caption prose, and the author-composite DX7 attribution should stay. The Zip100 caption is a useful ordinary example of preserving brand boundaries without erasing compatibility; Kobo/N64/GBC/GBA/GC captions similarly keep model/version simple and factual. The negatives about video standard, region, capacity and variant are necessary when front images cannot show them. 3DS event location remains separate from Japanese market chronology. Model 500 provenance keeps object-year 1951 separate from introduction and origin model; Picturephone caption names Mod II and period, avoiding genealogy collapse. AirPort multi-unit photo carefully isolates earliest graphite base, no confusing background comparators; Roomba’s no-mapping phrase is necessary. Quest3 sensor pattern, PSVR2 physicality and Vision Pro external form are visual matters, but function/chip/service require other evidence. Camera captions use a stable pattern: visible model label/control → illustrative comparison → a targeted exception (not Program, not package lens, not test results, not newer model). DCS100 caption explains combined camera/storage system without reducing it to a body alone. Xbox accessibility caption importantly avoids implying the pictured basic device encompasses every individualized accessory configuration. 5D Mark II text explicitly says frame cannot prove video/AF tests. Legion Go version boundary blocks same-brand successor confusions; G1 lens package and E-P1 add-on finder are separately qualified; X100 suffix generations named; K380 CJK legends are not globally universal. Newton museum number/H1000 and 1993 constrain model identity, while case remains an accessory shown rather than proof of bundled pack. Nintendo/Sony captions use silhouette for model-class recognition but explicitly keep regional shell variants distinct (Super Famicom vs SNES) and exact console generation (Switch before OLED/2, PS4 vs Slim/Pro, PS5 disc vs Slim/Pro). PSP region and Vita Japan launch cannot be inferred from pictured US/non-labelled units; RC-701 description uses historically specific “static video,” not digital-file terminology. Multi-view and region semantics are especially useful: COOLPIX 300 composite is same device, 900 is specific rotating lens, 15 controller separation is visually legible, original Ball is paired with manual while anniversary replica excluded. The Brailler status is deliberately pending, not a failure hidden by surrounding successes. RCA/Google Home/Nabaztag retain function boundaries and generation-specific cues. Nabaztag caption uses a visible generation cue and explicitly withholds an inference about legacy server operation. Quest, Ally, and Aibo entries are concise, object-led descriptions followed by narrowly targeted negatives (Quest 2 substitution, chip/test evidence, ERS-110/cloud state). PS5 Pro states the no-disc configuration and separates the license check from the visual claim; Claw identifies the blur as pre-existing and excludes performance-test use. Preserve these limits and the audit trail; they are not redundant caption padding. The VIVE caption carefully identifies a dated consumer model while excluding prototype and Pro variants. PS3/PS2 distinguish the photographed North American SKUs and bundled controller/expansion bay from launch-era regional configurations; embedded source marketing language (for example, sales superlatives) should not be carried into a visual claim. PS4 comparison caption maps visible three-tier/two-tier shells to Pro/Slim. Nikon F3 separates camera body from pictured lens and standard prism from HP; preserve the qualified visual identification rather than turning accessory presence into pack-in history. Steam Controller wording keeps capture date distinct from manufacture/launch; Portal limits screen text to the instant photographed; GR III is distinguished from IIIx by label/lens evidence. Echo caption correctly separates January 2015 EXIF from first publication and preserves a rejected possibly-rendered candidate as pending. Ally/X entry uses store placards to distinguish two contemporaneous models and explicitly records why the earlier white candidate was rejected. Keep pending status and provenance rather than smoothing uncertainty away. The correction note for the rejected Ally image is concrete and should remain attached to the choice. X5 caption balances source attribution with a visible marking limitation; case presence is not pack-in evidence. 2026 Controller is kept distinct from 2015, with photo date barred from proving batch. XL1 identifies PAL and avoids XL1s/XL2 substitution; TM5 names visible controls while disclosing crop/background processing. Hue clearly says two bulbs are not its three-bulb starter contents. These are concise provenance/representation statements, not unnecessary hedges. The Phantom sentence keeps the user-added GoPro external and separates it from the aircraft’s built-in configuration. LaserJet caption directs attention to the central exhibit and uses the visible no-Plus logo/1984 label while explicitly treating neighbors as scene background. Nest Protect describes the demo stand but refuses to infer sensor or current service operation. Braun distinguishes a model’s design year from the pictured specimen’s manufacture date. Preserve these distinctions because they prevent captions from converting exhibits into broader claims. PageBoy wording names the family/model code while explicitly disclosing the limited indexed excerpt and unavailable complete PDF; retain that evidence limit and the denial of date/function claims. Nest thermostat caption relies on physical installation details and chronology to distinguish an actual first-generation unit from later appearance. MX Master 3 attributes model identity to the image author and visible controls, while treating keyboard/wrist rest as props and the publication date as distinct from capture date. Those source qualifications are central to historical transparency. StanbyME Go’s caption distinguishes screen artwork from an actual turntable and identifies the scene as promotional; lack of a visible rear label limits any model/certification claims. Valve’s 2026 cube is distinguished from 2015 partner devices, with internals/performance explicitly outside the photo evidence. Virtual Boy stays pending because Japanese shop context does not establish regional SKU; preserve pending status. Access controller caption explains external assistive gear is an example configuration, not standard contents. T7 entry is careful about plain/Shield/Touch variants and capture date vs launch year. All retain evidence limits in direct language. The Freestyle caption names the model and visible support while treating people/set/projection as marketing context rather than an image-quality test. Galaxy XR identifies the Korean commercial launch setting and original two-angle JPEG, and explicitly separates it from Moohan prototype material. Preserve the original-file and licensing rationale; the notes distinguish the physical product claim from reuse provenance.
